Sprog
CR 2

Emerging from the shadows, you see a creature covered in matted, multicolored fur, its eyes glowing with a fierce, almost feral intensity. Standing at nearly five feet tall, the creature snarls, its claws flexing menacingly as it prepares to defend its territory.

XP 600
N Medium humanoid (sprig)
Init +2; Senses low-light vision; Perception +6

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 14, flat-footed 14 (+2 Dex, +2 natural, +2 size)
hp 19 (3d8+6)
Fort +5, Ref +5, Will +4

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft.
Melee 2 claws +4 melee (1d6+2)
Special Attacks Frenzy

STATISTICS

Str 14, Dex 14, Con 14, Int 8, Wis 12, Cha 6
Base Atk +2; CMB +4, CMD 16
Feats Weapon Finesse, Improved Initiative
Skills Knowledge (nature) +6, Perception +6, Stealth +8, Survival +6
Languages Common
SQ Low-light vision, spiritual essence, nature’s wrath, reversion

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Frenzy (Ex)

Once per day, a Sprog can enter a frenzied state for a number of rounds equal to 3 + its Constitution modifier. While in this state, the Sprog gains a +2 bonus to Strength and Constitution, a +1 bonus on Will saves, and a –2 penalty to AC. The Sprog cannot use any Charisma-, Dexterity-, or Intelligence-based skills (except Acrobatics, Fly, Intimidate, and Ride) or any ability that requires patience or concentration.

Spiritual Essence (Su)

Sprogs gain a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against death effects and negative energy effects.

Nature’s Wrath (Ex)

Sprogs gain a +2 racial bonus on Knowledge (Nature) and Survival checks.

Reversion (Su)

When a Sprog dies, they revert to an uncharged Nkisi. This Nkisi can be brought back to life by a Sprig Nganga through a special ritual (as described in the Nkisi of Life). The sprog would revert to sprig form, in this case.

Cure Light Wounds (Sp)

Once per day, a Sprog can use cure light wounds as a spell-like ability (caster level equal to the Sprog’s level).

ECOLOGY

Environment any forest
Organization Solitary
Treasure standard

Sprogs are the tragic result of a Sprig witnessing too much carnage at once, becoming stuck in a permanent Growth Surge.

These beings are larger and more aggressive than their Sprig counterparts, with a darker, more bestial appearance. Their bodies are covered in a riot of multicolored fur, creating a striking and somewhat intimidating appearance reminiscent of a vibrantly hued yeti. Their once child-like features contort into a more bestial visage, with sharpened teeth and fierce, glowing eyes. The once vibrant and multicolored fur becomes matted and dull, and their eyes, once filled with wisdom and wonder, now burn with a fierce, almost feral intensity.

Sprogs are often shunned by their Sprig communities due to their uncontrollable aggression and the danger they pose to others. They tend to live solitary lives, lurking in the shadows of the forests they once protected. Despite their isolation, Sprogs retain a deep, albeit twisted, connection to the natural world. They are driven by a primal urge to protect their territory, often clashing with other creatures that threaten their domain.
